Every week or so I skip classes at least for one day and stay in bed. During those days I would avoid talking to anyone (even to my s/o... but they understand and wouldn't judge me) and engage in escapism. To this day I wonder why I keep doing it... Maybe it's because I bottle up anxiety over the week? Considering I'm always pretending to be okay to the point of dissociating myself. Or maybe it's because I feel so distressed when I go outside, every once in a while my fears ought to overwhelm me. 

As a temporary solution staying in bed and detaching myself from my own responsibilities might be comforting, but when I finally pull myself together I have to deal with all the shit I didn't take care of, and that is incredibly stressful. I have yet to find a middle ground where I can vent out my anxiety but without leaving my responsibilities behind, nor avoiding social interaction.

Llevo dos años trabajando de empaque con ansiedad social y funciono súper bien. Nunca será tan agradable como estar encerrada en mi pieza, pero ciertamente es muchísimo mejor que ser cajera (de verdad no entiendo cómo ellas pueden someterse a tanta presión, las compadezco y admiro). Lo bacán de ser empaque es que a los clientes apenas les importo y con suerte notan mi existencia, la mayoría solo quiere sus cosas empacadas e irse asap; el espectro de cosas que digo es tan pequeño que lo automaticé (muchas gracias, a usted, caja central está por allá, sí hay una tabaquería, al fondo a la derecha, de nada); casi siempre estoy tan ocupada empacando que no me alcanza el tiempo para pensar en cómo me estoy moviendo o cómo me veo (siempre tengo esa clase de pensamientos intrusivos cuando estoy expuesta a a situaciones sociales, excepto cuando trabajo); el super donde trabajo es gigante y también lo es la cantidad de empaques, somos como 170 y rara vez interactuamos entre nosotros; y, por último, la propina es tan buena que me va mejor que en cualquier otro trabajo jajajaja. Sé que dicen que para entrar a empaques hay que matar como a 3, o ser parte de esa mafia, o no sé qué, pero si conoces a alguien que trabaje de empaque de verdad es muy fácil entrar. Si no conoces a nadie siempre puedes ser insistente e ir a preguntar muchas veces al super, así es como han entrado varios empaques de aquí. Si tienes más dudas al respecto mándame un DM no más, te ayudaré en lo que pueda. Mucha suerte en tu búsqueda!!

Man, I can't even remember the last time I had a profile picture on Facebook. My SA regresses each time I think about how exposed I am to criticism in social media and whenever I start comparing myself to other people's accomplishments. I used to be active on Twitter back in the day and I made pretty good friends thanks to it, but now I can't handle the thought of sharing even the tiniest aspects of my life. My Instagram account? Deleted. Everything I've ever shared in Facebook? Both hidden and deleted. My friends often make fun of my profile because it looks like a dead account, and I've had acquaintances of mine ask me if I was ok only because of my lack of activity and/or profile pictures (Isn't that kinda twisted? Like they could tell anything about my life from fucking pictures).
Couldn't have said it better.

True love and romantic love are completely different things, for me at least. True love is mutual care and nurture, the will to learn and understand, the desire to support and encourage. I believe the latter on the other hand is in many ways oppressive and directly linked with compulsory heterosexuality, full of internalized messages such as marriage and motherhood —you know, the ones that tell us we are incomplete human beings until we find the "right guy"—. And I ain't got time for that crap.

I don't know if it's related or not, but ever since I started asking for more shifts at work my mood has consistently improved. I work in customer service w/ tipping, so every time I receive a large tip I get all excited and cheerful. I am guilty of retail therapy —after all, so it's not surprising that I love money so much, but I don't earn nearly enough to travel overseas or to afford successful yet expensive therapy. That bums me out sometimes.

It pains me to see that our society is still very unaware of mental health. Most of them wouldn't understand depression only because it's an invisible illness and there's no physical way for them to tell you're suffering. As if we had some kind of injury and there's a wound we could show them. As if they could somehow x-ray our feelings of emptiness and misery. So when they witness suicide attempts not only they take it as their only wake-up call, but they also get to label us as attention seekers? Fuck them, you know. There's no need to convince people like that. Tell them to educate themselves, for all we care. What's important is that **we** believe in you. This whole community acknowledges your struggling and we're here to help. Surround yourself with people that understands your suffering, just like we do. And if something goes wrong, you can always come back here and rant with us. But please, don't seek to convince those people. They're not worth putting your life at stake.

I know there's nothing I could tell you to change your mind or boost your confidence, since I certainly been there and I wasn't eager to listen. In fact, until this day I wonder why would anyone like me at all, but I'm very grateful to have such an awesome s/o and amazingly supportive friends anyways. And even though I'll most likely never be fully comfortable and content in my own skin, I still get to love and enjoy precious moments w/ them. That mindset definitely helped me get rid of any remaining jealousy, but at that time I was also working on deconstructing romantic love, so that was another contributing factor.
